title: Datum handoff jotter
body:
Quick personal jotter for the 03/12 -> 03/13 night bridge. Not polished — carry-forward items and temporary fixes that might need formalizing into the real runbook.

Shift summary (short):
- Quiet first half; one noisy alert at 02:14 about elevated p99 on hosted-api-prod-us-east-1.
- Root cause: cache eviction thrash on model-quantized-v2 leading to repeated KV reloads on worker-7.
- Temporary mitigation: disabled model-quantized-v2 variant routing in smartrouter for the affected customer pool; lowered batch size for the pool to 8. Latency back to normal by 02:50.
- No active incidents now. Leaving notes for follow-up and cleanup.

Immediate items to pass on:
1) Worker health sweep: worker-7 (ip 10.12.7.198) shows high GPU mem churn in last 24h. Run: 
   - ssh gateway && ssh infra@10.12.7.198
   - docker ps | grep inference-worker
   - docker logs --tail 200 inference-worker | grep -i eviction
   - check /var/log/nvidia-smi-wrapper.log for OOM entries
   If logs show repeated KV cache thrash, create an internal bug with trace and attach last 1000 lines.

2) Smartrouter config rollback note: I flipped routing for 'customer-pool-b' to skip model-quantized-v2 at 02:32. The change is in the temporary routing bucket labeled 'tmp/2026-03-12-skip-qv2' in the console. Please revert only after the following are true:
   - Pod churn on worker-7 is stable for >= 2h
   - Perf SLOs at p95/p99 are under thresholds for 2 consecutive checks
   How to revert: Console -> Routing -> Buckets -> restore 'default-customer-b' and remove tmp bucket. Or use CLI: redwoodctl routing restore --bucket default-customer-b --from tmp/2026-03-12-skip-qv2

3) Deployment note: PR #482 (serving-runtime) was deployed at 01:10 with a small kernel-selection tweak. Seems unrelated but keep an eye on workloads with sequence lengths > 2048.

Known issues to track (not urgent):
- Eval reg: some evals on page-rewrite-task show slight decrease in ppl for model-ceres-3 at long context (opened ticket JIRA-1137). Might be quantization-related; work with Applied ML.
- Dedicated pool autoscaler: one spike early morning where scale-down happened while pending jobs existed. I added a temp guard to ignore pending job count < 3 for 30m. Need proper fix in autoscaler logic (ticket recommended).

Playbook snippets (quick commands):
- Check queue lengths: redwoodctl metrics query --name request_queue --window 15m --filter pool=hosted-api-prod-us-east-1
- Restart worker container (safe sequence):
   1) drain: redwoodctl worker drain worker-7 --grace 30s
   2) restart: sudo systemctl restart inference-worker || docker restart inference-worker
   3) undrain: redwoodctl worker undrain worker-7
- Remove temporary routing bucket: redwoodctl routing delete-bucket tmp/2026-03-12-skip-qv2 --confirm

Escalation contacts (order):
- On-call SRE: Ethan Brooks (pager duty) — PagerDuty: pd-ethan, Slack: @ethan.b
- Serving runtime eng: Priya Kapoor — Slack: @priya.k (for kernel/compilation concerns)
- Applied ML: Liu Zhang — Slack: @liu.z (for eval/regression questions)

Things I scribbled but didn't finish:
- Quick grep to find pattern of eviction: zcat /var/log/inference/*.log.gz | rg "KV_CACHE_EVICT" --line-number | tail -n 200 -> I started but aborted due to noisy logs.
- Could add a short test: run local sim with model-quantized-v2 at batch sizes 8, 12 to reproduce thrash. I left a script in my home dir: ~/scripts/sim-evict.sh (untagged, needs params)

Checklist before next shift (for me or whoever takes next):
- [ ] Attach worker-7 logs to JIRA-1137 if not already attached
- [ ] Open autoscaler ticket (or add notes to existing) with sample timeline and metric snapshots
- [ ] Re-check console routing buckets and remove tmp bucket when safe
- [ ] Ping Applied ML about the model-ceres-3 PPL drop and attach eval diffs

Loose thoughts / heuristics (notes to self):
- If we see p99 rise and infra shows >30% GPU mem churn across pool, likely KV eviction. Prefer temporary routing to skip heavy quantized variants rather than immediate restart.
- For customer-facing complaints, use canary fallback to v1 stable and enable structured logging for that org id to capture prompts causing large contexts.

Unresolved questions:
- Why did autoscaler decide to scale down despite pending jobs? Need to correlate scale decisions with queued jobs timestamp. Maybe a race in pendingJobs metric ingestion.
- Is the kernel-selection change in PR #482 causing any edge-case memory growth at long context? Priya to check.

Notes to tidy into formal runbook later:
- Template for routing temporary buckets and rollback checklist (procedural steps + safety checks).
- Standardized eviction detection query + alert that includes sample request IDs to repro.

Sign-off: I'm leaving the watch at 07:00 local. If anything noisy pops up, escalate via PD. Otherwise ping me in slack for clarifications.

-- Maya

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Might be worth adding a perf probe that simulates a 3-min sustained 1k token request to see KV thrash.
- Followup on PR #482: check CI perf job results (link above)
